intent: Pick one day or a date range from a calendar that opens in a popover from a trigger button or a typed field.
typical_uses: A form field or filter whose value is one day
A filter whose value is a start and an end date

dont_use_when.situation: A calendar that stays visible on the page instead of opening behind a trigger
A time of day, alone or next to a date

instead.note: DatePicker selects whole days only; a time goes in its own field, such as an Input with `type="time"`.

dont_use_when.situation: A date typed in free form or in words, or a typed date range

instead.target: a parser of the consuming application's own choosing feeding a plain Input
instead.note: The `input` variant accepts only its one display format and exists in single mode only; the kit ships no free-form date parser.

invariants.text: `open` and `defaultOpen` are both accepted; `defaultOpen` seeds the initial state and is ignored afterwards, and when `open` is given it wins and the component follows it on every render.

The picker holds no selection of its own: the trigger label and the calendar's selected days always come from `selected`, and a pick only calls `onSelect`, so a caller that does not store the value it receives sees the trigger and the grid keep the previous selection. In single mode, picking the day already selected calls `onSelect(undefined)`. The one selection-related local state is the `input` variant's typed text, which resyncs to `selected` whenever `selected` changes from outside to a different time value.

`variant` (default `button`) is declared only by the single-mode props and `numberOfMonths` (default 2) only by the range-mode props. The schema lists both as optional properties without tying either to `mode`, so `mode="range"` together with `variant` validates against it but does not type-check.

In single mode a picked day closes the popover unless `closeOnSelect` is false; in range mode the popover stays open unless `closeOnSelect` is true, and then it closes on every pick, the first endpoint included.

The calendar opens on the month of `selected` (of the range's start in range mode), including a value that arrives after mount; month navigation by the user holds until `selected` changes to a different time value. The comparison is by time, so a caller that builds a new Date for the same day on every render does not reset the month.

In the `input` variant, `onSelect` receives a date only when the typed text parses as a real date against the field's display pattern `MMMM dd, yyyy` in `locale` and carries a four-digit year; emptying the field calls `onSelect(undefined)`, and any other text calls nothing. ArrowDown in the field opens the calendar.
`locale` is passed to the calendar grid and also formats the trigger label, the typed field's text and the parse of what is typed, so a localized picker reads in one language throughout.
`disabled` is not applied to the trigger button or the typed field, which stay focusable and keep opening the calendar.

`id`, `className` and `aria-label` go to the trigger button in the `button` variant and in range mode, and to the text field in the `input` variant. In the `input` variant the trailing calendar button is named by `aria-label` when one is given and by `openCalendarLabel` otherwise, so a consumer `aria-label` names the field and the button alike. Without `aria-label` the trigger button is named by its text, the formatted selection or the placeholder.

anti_patterns.dont: Assemble a Popover, a Calendar and a Button by hand for a date field
anti_patterns.do_instead: Use DatePicker, which wires the open state, the visible month and the trigger label

anti_patterns.dont: Keep a separate text state next to the `input` variant to hold what the user is typing
anti_patterns.do_instead: Store only what `onSelect` delivers; the field keeps its own typed text and commits once the date is complete

selected.states: selected is the committed value, a Date or undefined in single mode and a `{ from, to }` date range or undefined in range mode
selected.because: `Date | undefined` on the single-mode props and `DateRange | undefined` on the range-mode props, discriminated by `mode`; the compiler emits one JSON type per property, and a Date object has no JSON Schema representation.

onSelect.states: onSelect is a callback called with the next value, typed like `selected` for the active mode, not a value
onSelect.because: `(date: Date | undefined) => void` in single mode and `(range: DateRange | undefined) => void` in range mode, discriminated by `mode` - functions, which no JSON Schema type covers.

onOpenChange.states: onOpenChange is a callback called with the next open state of the calendar popover, not a value
onOpenChange.because: `(open: boolean) => void` - a function, which no JSON Schema type covers.

disabled.states: disabled is the calendar's day matcher, one matcher or a list of them, that rules out the matching days
disabled.because: `Matcher | Matcher[]`, where a matcher is a boolean, a Date, a list of Dates, a range, a before/after bound, a day of the week or a function of the day; the compiler emits one JSON type per property, and Dates and functions have no JSON Schema representation.

locale.states: locale is a date-fns locale object
locale.because: `Locale` is an object holding a code, formatting and parsing functions (`formatDistance`, `localize`, `formatLong`, `match` and others) and week options; the functions have no JSON Schema representation.

container.states: container is the DOM node, shadow root or ref to one that the calendar popup portals into; an explicit null renders no popup until a node is passed
container.because: `HTMLElement | ShadowRoot | RefObject<HTMLElement | ShadowRoot | null> | null` - live DOM nodes and ref objects, which no JSON Schema type covers.

unexposed_parts.reason: Composed inside DatePicker as the open-state root; its open state is exposed as DatePicker's own `open`, `defaultOpen` and `onOpenChange`.
Composed inside DatePicker and rendered as the trigger Button, or as the `input` variant's trailing calendar button.
Composed inside DatePicker as the calendar's popup, made padding-free by date-picker.module.css; only its `container` is exposed, as DatePicker's own prop.
Composed inside the popup; besides the selection, only `captionLayout`, `disabled`, `locale` and, in range mode, `numberOfMonths` reach it from DatePicker.
Composed as the outline trigger with a calendar icon in its `icon` slot, or as the `input` variant's ghost icon button; neither takes a variant or size from DatePicker.
Composed as the `input` variant's text field, with the calendar button in its `end` slot.

good.title: One day, button trigger
good.code:
const [date, setDate] = useState<Date | undefined>();
<DatePicker selected={date} onSelect={setDate} />

good.title: A date range over two months
good.code:
const [range, setRange] = useState<DateRange | undefined>();
<DatePicker mode="range" selected={range} onSelect={setRange} />

good.title: A typed field with a calendar button, days before today ruled out
good.code: <DatePicker variant="input" selected={date} onSelect={setDate} disabled={{ before: new Date() }} />

bad.title: disabled used to switch the whole picker off
bad.why: `disabled` is the calendar's day matcher, so `true` rules out every day while the trigger stays clickable and keeps opening a grid with nothing to pick; it never disables the trigger.

bad.title: A made-up defaultSelected prop for an uncontrolled picker
bad.why: DatePicker has no uncontrolled selection: `selected` and `onSelect` are both required, and the value lives in the caller's state.
